mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 2.5% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day pre-increase average (t-test p > 0.05) during the same month.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.5% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that compress real equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to the 30-day pre-change average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS exceeding 10,000 jobs indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly increase > +10,000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically higher than the 30-day pre-strengthening average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (quarterly) grows by more than 5% from the prior quarter, it reflects robust business demand that elevates earnings expectations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive relative to the 15-day pre-GDPC1-growth average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (monthly) by more than 2% signals supply-side headwinds that compress industrial production capacity, raising uncertainty and depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during the INDPRO contraction are not statistically lower than the 25-day pre-contraction average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in HOUST (monthly) and FEDFUNDS (monthly) above their prior month averages jointly signal a dual pressure of strong demand and higher policy costs, which together depress S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: Dual pressure regime: demand expansion with restrictive policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to the 15-day pre-concurrent-increase average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE below 5% for two consecutive months indicates softening labor market pressures, lowering wage growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during the cooling period are not statistically lower than the 30-day pre-cooling average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of monetary easing (as signaled by FEDFUNDS < 1% and UNRATE > 6%), a sharp drop in RSAFS (monthly) below 400,000 indicates weakening demand absorption, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: Easing regime with weak demand absorption
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during the trigger event are not statistically negative relative to the 15-day pre-event average (t-test p > 0.05).
